title: wt sync rebase|resume|undo --json
description: What a wt sync rebase, resume or undo did. Printed by `wt sync rebase [<work>...] --json`, `wt sync [<work>...] --rebase --json`, `wt sync resume <work> --json` and `wt sync undo <work> --json` as the only thing on stdout, also when a handled SIGINT or SIGTERM ends it. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

schema.description: The major version: a new one only for a change that breaks readers.

schemaVersion.description: The full semantic version of this schema that the output follows.

command.description: The verb. sync rebase since 1.3.0: before it the verb was spelled wt sync run and named itself sync run. No wt prints sync run since 1.4.1; the value stays for results saved before it.

repo.description: The main checkout, as wt sweep --json names the repository; null when the verb stopped before reading it.

onto.description: The trunk commit rebased onto: after the run's fetch, or the one the handed-over run recorded. Null for undo.

trunkSync.description: What the run did to local trunk after its fetch, as for wt up. Null when it did not fetch, and always for resume and undo.

outcome.description: done: every participant rebased, fastForwarded, undone or skipped. refused: nothing changed, or error stopped the verb first. partial: something changed and not everything finished. interrupted: a signal ended it.

error.description: Why the verb stopped before touching any participant; for undo, also why it stopped after putting some back.

recovery.description: For interrupted: the way back wt printed.

trunkSync.description: Local trunk against origin/<trunk>, and what was done about it. See docs/json.md.

local.description: Local trunk after the run (as found unless fast-forwarded); null when there is none.

remote.description: The origin/<trunk> commit compared with; null when there is none.

localAhead.description: Commits local trunk has that origin lacks, as found.

remoteAhead.description: Commits origin has that local trunk lacks, as found.

skippedReason.description: Why local trunk was left; null when fast-forwarded or with nothing to do.

result.description: rebased, fastForwarded, rebasedStepFailed, needsRecovery, handedOver, interrupted and undone changed the branch or worktree; skipped, refused, notRun and restored left them as they were. fastForwarded (since 1.2.0): the branch was behind its own remote and has nothing to rebase at the remote's commit, so the run moved it there and that is all; after is that commit, pushCommand is null, undoCommand puts it back.

pushCommand.description: For rebased: the push, as an argv. Since 1.4.0 null also for rebased, when wt has no push to make or offer for the branch, which noPushReason explains.

noPushReason.description: Since 1.4.0: for rebased with a null pushCommand, why wt made and offered no push for the branch, in words, whatever the reason: among them that it tracks a remote branch of another name with nothing recorded for it, and that the branch of another name it is recorded as pushing to holds commits that cannot be shown to be old versions of its own. Null otherwise.

fixCommand.description: Since 1.4.0: the command that settles noPushReason, as an argv, when one does: wt sync push-to <branch> <remote>/<branch>, which records the branch it tracks as where it pushes. The same command with the branch's own name on the remote records that instead. It names no directory: run it in the repository. Null otherwise.

safetyRef.description: The ref pinning the branch's tip from before the run: refs/wt-sync/<branch>/<epoch>.

deferred.description: What each deferred step of a finished rebase came to.

result.description: owed since 1.5.0: not run, because a need of it did not answer its probe in a run started with --allow-owed; owed like a failed step.

reason.description: Why it failed, was skipped or is owed.

undoCommand.description: What puts it back where the run found it, as an argv; null when there is nothing to undo.

planFile.description: For handedOver: the plan file saying what is yours.

ownRemoteSync.description: Since 1.2.0. Always an object from wt sync rebase; always null from resume and undo, which do not check: the check ran when the run started.

checked.description: Since 1.5.0: how many replayed commits the each_commit checks ran at, in this run or this resume. 0 when nothing was checked.

checkFailed.description: Since 1.5.0: the each_commit check that stopped the rebase: handedOver at that commit, or restored for a stack parent. Null when none failed.

commit.description: The replayed commit it failed at.

error.description: What failed: an exit status, a timeout, or the tracked files it changed.

stack.description: Since 1.6.0: for a --stack run, the stack held on this worktree's line: its layers and what came of each. Null for any other run.

ownRemoteSync.description: Since 1.2.0: what the run found of a participant's own remote, the remote-tracking ref a push of its branch would replace, and what it did about it. See docs/json.md.

ref.description: The remote-tracking ref, as remote/branch; null only when no ref could be named.

state.description: As found, before anything moved; the states are those of ownRemote in wt status --json.

local.description: The branch as found, before any fast-forward: where wt sync undo puts it back.

remote.description: The remote commit compared with; null for none, gone and unknown.

localAhead.description: Commits only the branch had; null for none, gone and unknown.

remoteAhead.description: Commits only the remote had; null for none, gone and unknown.

fastForwarded.description: The run moved the branch from local to remote before rebasing it. It stays true as a record when the rebase after it was put back, which takes the branch back to local.

allowed.description: state is diverged and the run went on over it under --allow-diverged; false when the participant was refused for something else.

skippedReason.description: Why the own remote refuses the participant; null when it does not. diverged: --allow-diverged goes on. operation, dirty, session: behind, and it cannot be fast-forwarded. failed: the fast-forward itself did not go through; nothing of this participant was touched. fetchFailed: the branch's own remote could not be fetched, so the run could not look; trunk's fetch failing is the run's error instead.

stack.description: Since 1.6.0: a stack held on one line, for --stack: the line from where it leaves trunk (base) to its tip (head), and its layer branches, bottom first. See docs/json.md.

branch.description: The line's own branch: the worktree named.

base.description: Where the line leaves trunk: the merge base.

head.description: The line's tip before the run.

autosquash.description: A fold of the line's fixups onto its own base (--autosquash), not a rebase onto trunk.

refusal.description: The run's: why no layer moved: a new tip failed its check, or the fold changed the line's content. Null in the look, and when each layer was moved or held.

stackLayer.description: Since 1.6.0: one layer of a stack held on one line. The look fills what it sees; a run also fills what came of the layer, and those fields are null in the look.

commits.description: Its commits from the line's base, its tip included.

foundBy.description: tipOnLine: a local branch whose tip is a commit of the line. named: named with --layer.

worktree.description: The worktree the branch is checked out in; null when it is in none.

state.description: What holds the layer's worktree: none (in no worktree), clean (nothing), dirty (tracked changes), rebasing (a rebase in progress, there or in another worktree that will move it), bisecting (a bisect in another worktree started from it), busy or idle (an agent session), process (a process whose working directory is inside the worktree), unknown (it could not be read, which holds the layer). In a run, as read when the layer was moved.

stateDetail.description: Who or what holds it: the session, the process, or why it could not be read.

newTip.description: The run's: the layer's new tip, read from the rebase and checked. Null in the look, and when the run moved no layer.

commitsAfter.description: The run's: commits of the new tip from the new base, as the check compared them with the plan.

mapped.description: The run's: tip (the new tip is its own tip rebased), tipDropped (trunk already carries its tip; the new tip is its last commit left), emptied (trunk carries every commit of it; it ends where the layer below does).

patch.description: The run's: whether what the layer brings to the line is the same patch as before, by git's stable patch-id. Never a refusal.

patchWhy.description: The run's: why the patch changed.

result.description: The run's: moved (the branch is at newTip, its worktree reset with it), held (left where it was; held says why and moveCommand moves it by hand), unchanged (its new tip is its old one), planned (recorded and not moved: the moves stopped before it), moving (its move was under way when the moves stopped: undo puts its ref back), needsRecovery (a move that went part way and could not be put back: held says what to look at, the layer keeps its pins, and wt sync undo puts it back).

how.description: The run's: ref (a branch in no worktree, moved with update-ref guarded by its old tip), worktree (reset --keep in its worktree, under that worktree's lock).

held.description: The run's: why the layer was held, or for needsRecovery what to look at.

moveCommand.description: The run's: what moves a held layer by hand.

pushCommand.description: The run's: for a moved layer, its push to its own remote as an argv, with a lease on the commit wt last fetched there. A run does not push layers. Null otherwise.

noPushReason.description: The run's: for a moved layer with no safe push command, why: no remote branch of its own yet, or the remote has commits the branch never had.

note.description: The run's: what else happened to a moved layer, such as a checkout of it that landed during its move, at its new tip.

stackSkipped.description: Since 1.6.0: a branch on the line not taken as a layer: a backup name (wt refs sweep's patterns), which --layer takes.
